output.brief: The fall in first-contact resolution is most likely caused by the Finance credit-limit change on 14 April, not by the new starters. The in-call credit limit dropped from £100 to £25, and the billing system now refers larger adjustments to the Billing Resolution team. The share of billing calls referred rose from 7% to 54% in the same week. Referred calls resolve at about 34%, against 82% for the rest, and those rates did not change. The referral rate is about the same for new starters (56%) and experienced agents (53–54%). Experienced agents' FCR fell from 75% to 67%, the same as the site, so the April intake is not the cause. The tariff rise changed the call mix only slightly, and tariff calls still resolve at 85%. The IVR redesign and workload effects are not established. I'm fairly confident, but not certain. Don't put the April intake on performance plans, because their results aren't distinguishable from the rest. Agree a revised credit authority with Finance and trial it on two teams for six weeks, tracking FCR and unsupported credits. Ask MI to rerun the breakdown for those teams. Postpone the full dashboard rebuild.
